utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm going to get enough exposure in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: We try to rotate often enough to keep it confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, I do beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: With your permission I call the next witness, Mr. Fadil Kastrati.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Would you be good enough to read aloud the affirmation that is on the card given to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't receive the English translation on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let's hope the matter is now remedied.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Black is going to ask you some questions. Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kastrati.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can you understand me all right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'm sorry we kept you waiting yesterday and you didn't begin until today, but we'll try to move on as quickly as I can.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Before we begin let me say that if at any time you don't understand one of my questions, just please tell me and I'll try to state it more clearly. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: In a moment I'll ask you some questions about your personal background and about events in 1998, but before I do that I just want to ask you some preliminary questions. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Before coming to The Hague to testify today, did you attend an interview with a Prosecution investigator on 19 February 2004?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: But do you remember attending an interview with an investigator from this Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And at a interview did you answer the questions of your own free will?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I've answered the questions out of my own free will.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have some technical problems, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Please explain and we'll try to figure those out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Perhaps the problem was with the interpreters and not the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It seems we may be able to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we please ask the witness to speak, to check just if we can hear him properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please indicate again your name, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Fadil.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. That was just to test your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Witness, I'm sorry for the technical difficulties. If we could just continue. I was about to ask you if in your interview with the Prosecution investigator you answered the questions truthfully.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I've always tried to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And have you met with representatives of the Prosecution on any other occasion before you travelled here to The Hague this week?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes. They came to my house in Lipjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And did they discuss your testimony or another issue? Just please tell us what was talked about on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Do you refer now to our meeting in Lipjan or when they came to my house?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I just would like to know if you've discussed your evidence with investigators other than to make the travel arrangements to bring you to The Hague and those sort of details.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: We discussed my time in the war and some other everyday things.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And was this the interview in February 2004 or was this a different occasion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: It was -- now I don't remember whether it was February or another month. For me it wasn't a big deal. But this is when they came and asked me those questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. And did this just happen on one occasion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: It happened just on one occasion when I was questioned in Lipjan. And after that they came one or two more times to my house, asked me whether I was in danger, and I told them that I was not in danger and that there was no one that could put me in danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. And just before I move on -- and you and I met on Wednesday for a couple of hours to discuss your testimony. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: This Wednesday here?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Not yesterday but the day before.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: That's how it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kastrati. Now I'll move on to a few questions about your personal background. Is your full name Fadil Kastrati?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And your father's name is Nazmi?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Were you born on the 3rd of April, 1967, in the village of Vershec now called Blinaje?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I was born on the 3rd of April, 1967, in the village of Vershec now called Blinaje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And that is in the Lipjan municipality in Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And you are Albanian; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Kastrati, please tell us how many years of education you received.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I've completed nine years of education.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And did you perform military service with the Yugoslav army in 1988?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I have not finished it -- I did not finish it. I just served two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can you explain why that was?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: They would be able to give you a better explanation because I want to complete my military service, but they said to me, no, that's enough for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Kastrati, after your military service with the Yugoslav army, did you ever live or work outside of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And just tell the Judges briefly when that was.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I worked in Germany sometime in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And had you worked in Croatia for a time as well, maybe that was before your military service?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, I worked in Croatia sometime between 1983 and 1985.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Kastrati, did you also work as a taxi driver in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I worked as a taxi driver before the war and I still do the same thing now after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: In the time before the war, did you ever -- as a taxi driver, did you ever have any problems with the Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, I had problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could you please briefly explain to the Trial Chamber the circumstances of those problems.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, I can explain. When I worked as a taxi driver, I don't remember the exact year when it happened, but I know that some things that I remember very clearly happened. The Serbs were just looking to close all the roads for us. There was no open road for us that they would allow us to use. They would stop the buses and did not let the pupils go to school, so we were forced to take the pupils to school with our vans. A person called Stola, I will never forget this name, he cursed me in Albanian and ordered me not to transport any passengers. He ordered me to go and get my documents. I knew that they were going to behave badly, but I had no other choice but to go and get my documents. When I went for the documents at their office, they beat me till I lost consciousness, till I was no longer aware what was going on with me. One grabbed me by the hair and hit me on the car, and the others were also hitting me without stopping. I found myself in the hospital. I don't know who brought me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What kind of injuries did you receive from this beating?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I had brutal injuries. My body suffered more injuries, my face as well. After several -- after few days I again started to drive, and the same persons behaved badly again, their colleagues as well. They seized my documents. At that time there was an Albanian who was a policeman and who worked with them; his name was Fatmir. With my friends, we were deliberating whether to call on this Fatmir or not. We thought that since he was Albanian he would be able to help us. But he did not help us. And eventually when we got our documents back, they just threw them at us and they did not beat us on that occasion. It's then when I told my friends, Let's get out of here because there is -- there are no conditions for us to work here any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kastrati. Now I want to turn your attention to the year 1998. When did you first hear about the Kosovo Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: For the first time I heard about the KLA when the Prekaz battle Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. took place with Adem Jashari.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember when that was approximately?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Approximately in March, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And what was your reaction when you heard about what happened to Adem Jashari?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: My interest was to find out about the war more and more because I was anxious to grab the arm and the weapon and join the liberators of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you join the KLA at that time?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: At that time I did not join because I didn't know anyone. I wanted to join the KLA but I did not join it at that time. I joined it a bit later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: When did you join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I joined the KLA on the 9th of May, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And I'd like you to explain to the Trial Chamber what happened on the 9th of May, 1998, that led you to join the KLA.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: If you could please repeat your question. I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Of course. Just tell the Judges what happened on the 9th of May, 1998.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Do you mean what happened in combat or what happened that made me join the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Let's start with what made you join the war.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, I had a great wish to join. This was a discussion amongst several friends, regardless of where to join, we just wanted to join. On 9th of May some friends of mine came. One of them had some connections with a person who knew where the combat was going on. And on the 9th of May there was combat in Lapusnik and we joined the combat, and that's how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: How did you learn about the combat in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: We live nearby. As the crow flies it's about 5 kilometres, not more than that. In a way we gave our word that we will join the war when it comes to it. So we joined it when the war came and we gave our contribution as much as we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You mentioned that you live very near to Lapusnik. But were you told that there was combat there or did you find out in some other way?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: A friend of the two friends that I went with came. His name is Ymer Alushani. He sent some persons who I didn't know who took us and asked us whether we wanted to join, because they knew that we wanted to join. So they asked us and we said yes, we will join the war and -- regardless of whether we will die or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Please tell the Judges who Ymer Alushani was.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Ymer Alushani was a fighter and a very brave person. I didn't know him from before. I can say that I first met him in the beginning of the war. He was a very brave man, a very brave fighter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And who are the other two friends that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: The other two friends are from my village. Their names are Fadil and Islam, Fadil Qadraku and Islam Qadraku. They are not my friends, they are just my co-villagers. We call ourselves between us uncles, but we don't know whether we have any family relationships. They did have some connections with the war, so I wanted to join the war and regardless of who the person was who had connections, it didn't matter to me. I just wanted to join.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And you told us that you went with those two people to join the war. Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: That's how it was. We went to the house of Ymer Alushani, and later we set off for Lapusnik at the rock location and that's where we took up our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember what time of day it was when you arrived in Lapusnik at this rock location?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: When I arrived at Lapusnik, it wasn't daytime, it was night. During the day there had been fighting, but personally I didn't get to -- arrive for that fighting during the day. I arrived there just before dusk.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: How did you though there had been fighting during the day?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: As I said, firing could be heard; I didn't know from where. But I just knew that there was fighting going on. And when the friends came and informed us, that's when I set off myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: When you set off for Lapusnik, were you armed?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What kind of weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: At that time I had a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What about your friends, did they have weapons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, they had weapons, too. One had an automatic rifle and the other a rifle. I don't know exactly, but I think it was a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You mentioned that you took up positions at the rock location in Lapusnik. Could you describe where that is in Lapusnik, perhaps in relation to any main roads in the area.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes. The Komorane-Peja road is nearby. And there on the top there's a rock. The Serb forces were positioned there, and in combat with the KLA they had to withdraw. And then I don't know where they went to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Just to be clear, which side of the Komorane-Peja road were you on?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: On the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Is that the left side -- if you're travelling in which direction?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: When you come from Komorane and in the direction of Peja, it's on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Why did you take up positions at the rock? Why did you choose that place?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I did not choose it. My friends chose it. It was a position from where you could clearly see the Serb positions; that's why I positioned there and that's why I stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Which friends were with you -- who was with you at that time when you arrived at the rock?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: At that time with me were Ymer Alushani, Islam Qadraku, and some others whose names I didn't know because I didn't know them at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Were there other soldiers -- were there other KLA soldiers in Lapusnik when you arrived besides those you've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, of course there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can you estimate about how many there were on that first day?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Approximately on that day there were about 20. I have seen this much. Maybe there were more in the mountains, but I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did that number change in the following days?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes. It grew every day bigger and bigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. What did you do when you arrived at the rock location?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: On the first day, so it's the 10th of May, during the day there was no fighting, no combat. We were just observing the area to see whether Serb forces were coming into our direction. Our aim was not to allow them to approach our population. Sometime in the evening, the Serbs were firing at our direction with heavy weapons and I don't know what else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: When the Serbs fired at you with heavy weapons, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: When they were firing at us, we were taking positions so that they could not reach us, hit us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And in the following days, what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: We were surveying the terrain. And when there was combat, although we wanted to fight and we were ready to fight, we could just give the maximum that we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you participate in any fighting during those first few days?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I tried to take part at all times, but sometimes it wasn't possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I understand that. You say that you "gave the maximum that we could." What were you able to do?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Well, they were firing at us and we were responding to that fire. We were trying to hit them; now maybe we have, but we couldn't see it from the distance. The fact is that we did fire at them as they did fire at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Kastrati, other than Ymer Alushani, Fadil Qadraku, and Islam Qadraku, do you remember any of the other people you saw in Lapusnik on those first few days?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing a person who I knew. There were many soldiers from the area, but I don't think I knew any of them. Because, for example, if you were now soldiers of the KLA, I don't know them. That's the same thing, I didn't know anyone there either.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: But was there anyone that you saw that stood out to you in the first day or two that you were there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes. I saw on the first day when Fehmi Lladrovci the commander was, and I took my oath before this man, before this great man. I was sincere in my wish to fight. And when I encountered such commanders, such great men, this wish grew bigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You say you took an oath before Fehmi Lladrovci. Can you describe how that happened?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes. When we took the oath, it was several of us, some friends of mine who I mentioned earlier and for whom that I said I didn't know. He addressed us with the words, now, sons, you have come here to fight. It's better that you go home because this is a big war and it requires boldness. But as for myself, when I heard these words this just encouraged me more and more. He was fighting together with his wife, so what can I say more about this great man?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember where this happened, where you took this oath?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: It was in Lapusnik in a house where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can you describe the house at all?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I don't know how to describe it. Orally perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes. I was just wondering if you remember how many floors it had, if it was old or new, any details that you remember.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: It was a house. I can't call it either old or new. It was one floor. It was near the road that leads to the rock location.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you ever go to this house on other locations besides the time when you took the oath?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I went to this house on one more occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What did you do on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I didn't do anything. I just wanted to meet the commander. I was in Blinaje and I did not find him there, and then I just returned home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll get to that in a moment. Do you know if the -- if any other soldiers used this house or went to this house?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, of course there were other soldiers there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Well, I mean on other occasions besides that oath ceremony. Did other soldiers use that house on other occasions?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: No, no. There weren't any.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Maybe there were, but I haven't seen any.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You told us that when you first arrived in Lapusnik you went to the rock. Did you go to other places in those first few days that you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. were there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Besides the rock -- so the first two days, I spent them at the rock. And later on, we came a little bit downhill towards the Komorane road where it was a little bit more flat. We stayed there for another two nights.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And what did you do at that location?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: The same as at the rock. We observed and then when there was fighting, we fought. But at that time there was no fighting; we only observed, we only surveyed the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Were there any fortifications of any kind in Lapusnik? By that I mean were there any trenches, any bunkers, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: There were bunkers. There were bunkers. The villagers helped us and we helped the villagers. Those where we had our positions and we could keep watch on the enemy from those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: With the help of the usher at this time, Mr. Kastrati, I'm going to show you a sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours and for the record, this bears the ERN U007-9681.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Kastrati, if you could look to your left and just take a moment to look at this sketch that I've given you. Mr. Kastrati, have you seen this sketch before?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And can you orient yourself all right there? For instance, can you see where the Komorane-Peja road is on that sketch?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we ask the witness to keep closer to the microphone. We can't hear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And also perhaps on our monitors if the audio/visual booth could zoom out so we can see more of this sketch.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is this one here I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. And you see there's a place where five roads come together. Do you see that spot there, Mr. Kastrati?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes. The one here you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes. What I'd like you to do -- and actually I'll ask the usher to give you a pen. Do you see the rock position that you've mentioned on that sketch?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And could you put a number 1 by that, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And you mentioned another place that you went and spent the second and third day. Can you find that place on the sketch?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Please put a number 2 at that place.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Kastrati, you can see that on this sketch there's the word I believe "position." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you know who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: It's me. I -- it looks like my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And did you write that at the interview with the Prosecution investigator, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Of course, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned another location, the house, where you had the oath with Fehmi Lladrovci. Can you find that place on the sketch.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: It's approximately here, somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can you please put a number 3 at that location.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I think we're finished with this sketch. If it could be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're most welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And now again with the assistance of the usher, I'd like to hand the witness an aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: This is image 8 from Prosecution Exhibit P1, but the red markings that are in the maps booklet have been taken off. Mr. Kastrati, again I'd like you to just take a moment again to look at that photograph. Do you recognise the area depicted in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I don't know Lapusnik, the village, very well, but I remember the roads where I went. And I told you this yesterday as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Could you show the Judges any of the roads that you went that you remember.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes. This road you can see here. I think it's the asphalted road, Pristina-Peja. But the road I took with my friends or sometimes on my own. It's this one here. And this part here is called Komorane Nalte. I went here to Kishna Reka, Nekovce, and arrived here and moved up here. There were bunkers here and positions. We called this road Te Vllecat.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Can you find on that photograph the place that you said you went on the second and third days.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters are having a problem with microphones again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even yesterday I told you I couldn't figure out exactly where it was, but I think it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: There are many roads. I'm not so sure about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: It's a bit confusing. But can you find on this map near the middle the place where the five roads come together?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I'll try. I don't know if I'll be able to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: It's fine. Just see if you will be able to.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I think somewhere here, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the five roads, the four positions, the four positions? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Yes exactly. Can you point to that location again?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Okay, okay. Because I was thinking about something else. It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Could you put a number 2 at that location, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And before we move on I forgot to ask you to, if you could, show the Judges with the pen again the route that you took going to Lapusnik that you showed us just a minute ago. If you could mark that on the photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: You mean the road I took? Would you like me to write a number or show you which route I took?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: I'd like you to put a number 1 next to the route, and then with the pen just draw the route that you followed.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Now, I know that you've said that you're having a little trouble with the photo, and that's understandable. Can you find on here the house where you took the oath before Fehmi Lladrovci? Just see if you can.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I tried earlier to find it. I don't know the village very well; that's why it's a little bit of a problem for me. But in the sketch you showed me earlier it was easier for me to find it. So I'll tell you approximately because I don't know where exactly it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Tell us approximately, if you can. If you can't, that's fine, just say so.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I think it was somewhere here. If the rock is here, somewhere here, the house should be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Could you put a number 3 there, please, about where you think it was.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I think it is here but I'm not sure. I'm looking at the roads here that lead to the rock. It might be here, but as I said I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could have an exhibit number for this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, that will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kastrati. I'd like to keep your attention focused still just on those first few days you were in Lapusnik. You said that you arrived in Lapusnik with some friends, Ymer Alushani, Fadil Qadraku, and Islam Qadraku. Did you see them again during those first few days?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: The first day I saw them and I saw them now and again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: But I did not meet them during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You say you saw them now and again. Do you mean also on those first few days that you were in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes. I mean the first days, that's when I saw them occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember what they were doing those times that you saw them?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Well, just like any other soldier. They were doing the same thing, defending the people and caused damage to the enemy as much as possible. That is what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Were you in Lapusnik still on the 12th of May, 1998, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember attending any other meetings besides the oath that you told us about in front of Fehmi Lladrovci while you were in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: No, I never had any meetings, and I was not interested to go to meetings. I just wanted to go to war to fight. I don't know whether there were any meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. We've been focused on the first few days, but at some point did you leave Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: How did that come about? Why did you leave?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I did not want to leave, but Commander Fehmi Lladrovci, he said that it's better for you to go and observe, keep watch on the village where I lived, Blinaje, how many enemy forces go in there and how many get out. And that's why I went there and kept watch there. And when there was fighting, when I could I went to Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And did Commander Fehmi Lladrovci tell you this personally, that it was better for you to go to Blinaje and monitor enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Was anyone with him when he told you that or was he alone, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I was alone when he said those words to me. And later he gave me Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. a soldier, Islami, he was a co-fighter. And he gave me that soldier because he knew people who dealt in guns. And when we were able we brought guns and weapons. He knew where he got those weapons. When we could, we brought those guns to the soldiers, to Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Just to be clear, is that the same Islam you mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember how many days after you arrived in Lapusnik it was that you went back to Blinaje?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Approximately three or four days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And what did you do in Blinaje?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: When I went to Blinaje, I stayed at home so that other people would not know that I was involved in the war because it was dangerous for my family. I went up a mountain. I could see them and they could not see me. They might have seen me, but I was a civilian and they did not know what I was doing. And I -- when there were forces that came to that place, I had to wait to see whether they were -- would stay there or leave. Sometimes they would stay. And when they did that, in the evening I took my car and went to Lapusnik to Fehmi Lladrovci and told him about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Just to be -- to have a clear record, you say that you could see them and they could not see you. Who was they? Who do you mean by "they"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: By "they" I mean the Serbs. We called them Shkji or Serbs as you call them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: When was the first time that you took your car and went to Lapusnik to tell Fehmi Lladrovci about what you'd seen?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date, but approximately two or three days after.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. And what happened on that occasion? Describe it for me, please, when you arrived in Lapusnik I mean.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: When I went to Lapusnik, there was not heavy fighting there, only sporadic fighting. I did not meet the commander, so I had to join the fighting. And then I met Commander Fehmi Lladrovci and he said, It's okay. There's been a car -- an APC with policemen, but they have left. So it's okay. But we will come to that area, we will.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you speak with Fehmi Lladrovci in person on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes. On this occasion, yes. And I remember it very clearly that on this occasion I spoke to Commander Fehmi Lladrovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember where you spoke with him?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: It was near the first positions where the bunkers were, in the mountain -- on the mountain somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you go to Lapusnik to report on any other occasions?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: There was another occasion, maybe two, I'm not sure. But I could not meet Fehmi Lladrovci on those occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Please tell us what happened on those occasions.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: The other occasions -- when I was in Blinaje, I told you earlier the -- they had their own purposes when they provoked us, I mean the Serbs. They came there with two APCs. They came and some of them tied handkerchiefs on their heads and kept their guns very obvious for the people to see and get scared. Sometimes one of the APCs stopped there and the other one left. Sometimes both of them stayed in the village overnight and left the next day, the next morning. These were the things that I had to report to the commander. But when I went to meet him, sometimes he was not there; I was not able to meet him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What did you do if you were not able to meet the commander?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: When I could not meet the commander, I had to meet Ymer Alushani because he said to me, Nobody has to know about these things that I'm telling you. If I'm not here, you tell those things to Ymer Alushani. So I had to meet Ymer Alushani. And that day I met Ymer Alushani and I told him about the things that happened in the village of Blinaje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember where you met with Ymer Alushani on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I met Ymer Alushani somewhere near those five roads where they meet. Those were the positions. I did not ask him where he was because it was not my duty or task to ask him where he was. I asked one of the soldiers, Is the commander here? And he said, No. And then I asked about Ymer Alushani. And I said, Is Voglushi here? And he said, Well, I'll go and fetch him for you. The soldier went and fetched Voglushi. And I explained to him everything that had happened in Blinaje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Just to be clear, is Ymer Alushani and Voglushi the same person?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, the same person. It was his nickname; Voglushi was his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. And other than Ymer Alushani, I asked you before if you'd seen the other friends that you arrived with, if you'd seen them in the first days at Lapusnik. Did you see those friends on any of these occasions that you returned to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Kastrati, when you first went from Lapusnik to Blinaje, were there other KLA soldiers in Blinaje besides you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: There was one other soldier, but I don't know what his tasks were, what the commander had told him. He was in the part -- he was in the lower part of the asphalted road; I was in the upper part. He did not need to come to my part and I did not need to go to his part. Each of us had their own tasks that -- assigned by the commander. I never asked him what your tasks are and he never asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. You've mentioned an asphalted road. Could you tell us more specifically which road you mean. I just wasn't clear on that.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: The road that goes from the rock to Blinaje --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, Magure to Blinaje.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My house is on the right side of the road and his house is on the left side of the road. The road is Magure to Blinaje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And who was this other person? Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Islami.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And this is the same Islam that you'd mentioned before. Correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Was there ever a time when the KLA established a larger presence, when more KLA soldiers came to Blinaje?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Could you repeat it again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Of course. Did the KLA eventually establish a larger present in Blinaje?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Later there were more soldiers, but I did not tell them that I was a soldier as well. I was a normal villager for them. After a week I asked the people in Lapusnik to go to Blinaje because I knew the area and I could do more in Blinaje than I could in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And were you allowed to go to Blinaje?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Who gave you permission to go to Blinaje?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I went to Lapusnik for a week or two, because in January the army was in Blinaje. I met Ymer Alushani in Lapusnik, and I said to him, Fehmi Lladrovci is not here so I can't meet him. But who is the person responsible here that can let me go to Blinaje? I know the area very well, I know the people, and I can do more there than here. And he said, Well, I'll go and ask somebody about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Who did he go and ask, do you know?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Now I know, but at that time I didn't. His name was commander. That's how we called him. And we did not ask about each other, especially the soldiers did not ask -- were not allowed to ask who that person was. When commander -- the name "commander" was mentioned, we respected that commander, whoever that person was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. But this commander in particular, do you know who that was? Do you his name or his nickname?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Now I know who the commander was that allowed me to go to Blinaje; it was Commander Qerqizi. And he said, You soldier, you must help us here. It would be better if you helped us here, but no problem. And I told him, Yes, I can stay here but I know the area there better, Commander. At that time I called him "commander," I did not know his nickname or name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And when was that you spoke with Commander Qerqiz?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: This was approximately two months later, two months from the time I got involved in the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: So two months after the 9th of May. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know when you'd like to take a break. This is a fine or I can continue if you prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Another 10 to 12 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Kastrati, then -- were you then allowed to transfer to Blinaje?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes. I was allowed by the commander and I had a great wish to go to the part of the world where I lived, because I knew the terrain better there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: How many soldiers were based in Blinaje when you transferred there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: When I went to Blinaje, in the beginning there were approximately 30 or 40 of them. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And did that number change while you were there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: How did it change?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I can easily say that the number grew every day, but I did not know how many soldiers there were and how many came. But there were many soldiers; that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And when you transferred to Blinaje, who was in command there?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: When I went to Blinaje, the commander at the time was a co-villager of mine; his nickname was Dardani. And my brother and his friend was Commander Blini. And I asked them to become a soldier with them, with their troops. They laughed a little bit and they said, Okay, of course, but you cannot go and fight; you're not brave enough. And I said, Well, I would like to try. And they said, Okay, you can join then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you know what the positions of Dardan and Blini were? And by that I mean their titles or their ranks.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: At that time and up until the end I can say I did not know what their rank was, but the soldiers said "commander." And when the word "commander" was mentioned there was respect for those people and there was discipline. It was not up to me to ask what their rank is and who you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Perhaps I didn't ask my question very clearly. Do you know what their responsibilities were? Let's take Dardan. Do you know what his responsibilities were?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I did understand the question well and I said he was a commander to me. He was a commander of the group of soldiers that were there, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. while Commander Blini, he explained it to me but I was not very clear. He said he was the commander of the operational zone. And I asked him, What is this operational, what does that mean? And he laughed and he said, You don't understand things. And I said, Well, I don't understand things, that's true, but I know how to fight against the enemy and I know how to defend my population, my people. He said that my task was to -- because he was also an officer in the 7th Army, he had experience, he had experience of trenches and bunkers. And that's where he worked and he had that responsibility. And the villagers, we -- all the villagers helped him. We tried to face up to the enemy as much as we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Kastrati, the translation that we got said Blini was the commander of the operational zone, but then you say operational -- did you mean operational zone or operations?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I say he was an operational commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I would like to add -- I don't know what this means, the word means, but when we were at home sometimes we talked to each other and he told me -- he tried to explain, but I don't know what these words mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: That's okay. Do you know who was the commander above Dardan and Blini?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I think it was Shukri Buja. I used to think that, but there was a Commander Luani as well. Both of them were commanders. I don't know what their activities were, what their positions were. As I said, I respected everybody who was called a commander. And if any of those commander -- any of those commanders would tell me to go to the Serbian checkpoint, I would go to the Serbian checkpoint without any doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander above Shukri Buja and Commander Luan?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I said it earlier. At that time I did not know, but now you know and I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And who is that -- who was it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: It's the gentleman over there, Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next topic is a little bit longer. Perhaps this is a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn until 10 minutes to the hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Mr. Kastrati, just before the break you told us that Fatmir Limaj was the commander above Shukri Buja and Commander Luani. How did you learn that Fatmir Limaj was their commander?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I learned this by listening to you and to many of my friends. I learned that he was the commander of the brigade. At that time, the name "brigade" was not mentioned; nothing was mentioned at that time. At that time only the Kosovo Liberation Army was mentioned as a term.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Have you ever personally met Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Before the war or after the war or during the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: At any time.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I met him once during the war. I knew that it was him -- in fact, in the beginning I didn't know who he was. But later I found out that it was Commander Celiku.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. Please tell us what happened on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Shall I go a little bit back in time or refer to the occasion when I met Commander Celiku?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: You can go a little back in time if it's necessary to explain it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: When I was at the positions in Blinaje, at that time it was necessary to remain with one unit. But as soldiers we were very tired, and in the meantime we were assisted by the villagers. Their hunting rifles would occasionally replace our weapons. In this way they helped us to prevent any Serb from coming to our direction. In the meantime, one of the villagers looked to me as a person who was trying to disturb the peace and order. As the Serbs were very close to our location, I said to this co-villager not to speak in a loud voice. And he replied, This is not your business. If you are now carrying a gun, it doesn't mean that you are something to me. And I said to him, Of course I know that I'm not something for you, but you should keep your voice down. And I said, Shut up, because if you continue you will have to go home then. And then he said to me, No, you cannot take my weapon. These are the words that we exchanged. I thought that he was crossing the limit, since the enemy was very close, and I thought that he was causing a damage and risk for us and for the villagers. There was a meeting held in our village. I did not take part in this meeting and I don't remember when it was held. This person raised this issue during the meeting with Commander Shukri Buja. And how this issue reached Commander Celiku I don't know, whether he reported it in person or the other reported it, but I know that it became known. There were many other soldiers there. Nobody had ranks and nobody knew who was a commander. To my misfortune, Mr. -- Commander Celiku came and he asked me, Are you Fadil Kastrati? I replied, Yes, that's me. He said to me, You, sir, have to be unarmed. It was very difficult for me when I heard these words. I'm very sorry, but I very -- I was very cross at him. But now I'm convinced that he was right and I have a deep respect for him and for any other soldier of the KLA. I asked him, Is it possible for you, commander, not to unarm me because I took up this weapon with a great will and wish. There are just a scarce number of KLA members here, and there's no need for you to unarm me. He said to me, It's not up to you to speak. I know when I should unarm you or when I should not unarm you. You disturbed the order in the village and the discipline here. I said to him, No, I did not cause a disturbance, but I just reminded that person that he should not speak too loud because it can be -- it can harm our soldiers. Commander Celiku said to me, You have to be unarmed because there are regulations and discipline in the ranks of the KLA. And for that discipline, we have to act this way. And if we allow these small mistakes to take place, it's better that you don't have a weapon. And this was it. He did not proceed with this matter. I met my brother there. I said to him, Baca Gani, please help me with the commander because I don't know him. If he unarmed me I don't know where to go. 15 days were too long for me to wait. I don't know whether he went to speak with the commander or not. I asked him to make a plea with the commander to allow me to fight at least during fightings and combat. So he allowed me to take the weapon and fight during fighting. And when the fighting seized, I was supposed to leave the weapons at the positions and go home. At that time I did not say this to him, and now he is able to hear it. Commander Dardan and Commander Blini did not tell him, Mr. Commander, I did not remain unarmed for 15 days but just for nine days because my brother, his friend, and our co-villager, they did not tell the commander but they gave me back my weapon after nine days. When I got my weapon back, I just don't know how to describe this event; it was a great thing for me to be able to face the enemy again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kastrati. Do you remember when the Lapusnik gorge was re-taken by the Serbs at the end of July 1998?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I remember, although I was not there, I was in Blinaje. But I heard that the Lapusnik gorge was overtaken by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: This time when you met Commander Celiku, Fatmir Limaj, was that before or after the Lapusnik gorge was overtaken by the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: This happened before, before the Lapusnik gorge was overtaken by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember how long before?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I can say that it was approximately a month or a month and a half. I did not take dates down. I was not interested in dates. My -- I was mainly preoccupied with fighting. I wanted to be a good KLA soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you know where Fatmir Limaj was based during this time when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Did you ever have any dealings with Fatmir Limaj after this incident?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any dealings with him, but it is possible that we were in a fighting together and that I did not recognise him. And to tell you the truth, I was very cross at him at that time and I didn't want to see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember when you learned that his real name was Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: At the time when he unarmed me I learned his name as Commander Celiku, and for me it was a great name. But I will say again that at that time after this I did not want to see him, I was thinking, maybe I again did a mistake and maybe he will unarm me again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Do you remember when you learned that his name was Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Sometime when the liberation army were -- when members of the liberation army came to The Hague, and that's when it was brought up that Commander Celiku's name was Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Okay. You've told that you were in Lapusnik for a few days around the 9th of May, 1998, and that you visited on a couple of occasions after that. Did you ever hear of a camp or a place in Lapusnik were people were held by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: No, I never heard of it. I heard about prisons, but not for this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: What did you hear about other prisons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I heard that there were prisons at the police station in Magure, in Lipjan, and that they were all covered in the blood of the Albanians. I was myself in one of them. I didn't hear of a prison in Lapusnik where you think. I don't know that there was one there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: And just to be clear, these other prisons you've mentioned, were those Serb prisons?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: But did you ever hear about the KLA arresting or detaining anyone, Serbs or Albanians, in May, June, or July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Please, I mentioned it before but I will repeat it again. I never heard that there was a prison in those parts that you're mentioning. My preoccupation was to fight, and I think that those participants in the war, they dealt with combat and not with arrests and imprisonments. I say this with full responsibility because we Albanians have been in prison always. My father, my grandfather, great- grandfathers, to this date. So we did not have to deal ourselves with such matters. Our duty was to support our people and not to arrest them. I never heard that there was a prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kastrati. I have no further questions for you at this time. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Black. Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Mr. Kastrati, my name is Karim Khan and I represent Mr. Fatmir Limaj. I have a few questions for you, but hopefully I will not be too long. You say that you joined the KLA after the battle of Prekaz. Just to be clear, that was after the killing of Adem Jashari. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And it was after Adem Jashari was killed that you realised that war was inevitable. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And when you went to Lapusnik by the rock on the 9th of May, 1998, you had come from your home and you were in civilian clothes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And apart from two months of national service, you had no military experience at all, did you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: No, I didn't. But during that time I learned a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Were you forced to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Did Ymer Alushani threaten you at all that if you didn't join the KLA something bad would happen?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: No, not at all. On the contrary, he would hug me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And whilst you were by the rock and whilst you were around Lapusnik, you say that the overall commander was Fehmi Lladrovci. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I heard, as I mentioned earlier, I heard him just as a commander. And now I realise that it was Fehmi Lladrovci, although he did introduce himself while we, the army, were present there in a guest-room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes. But who did you think was more important, Fehmi Lladrovci or Ymer Alushani? Who was the higher --

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: For the moment I thought it was Ymer Alushani, but later I realised that Lladrovci was a real man, although Ymer Alushani was not a man either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And whilst you were in Lapusnik, who was trying to organise things?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I said this before; I will repeat it. In the beginning of the war, during the first day when I myself didn't know how things will proceed from there, it seemed that it was Ymer Alushani together with 10 to 15 other persons. And in the meantime that day, Fehmi Lladrovci, the commander, came. So that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And you say that the Serbs opened fire with heavy weapons in Lapusnik. Do you know what type of heavy weapons were used or not?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: You are referring to the first day, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: When we discussed with the soldiers, they were saying that they were anti-aircraft weapons. I don't know how exactly they called them, but I know that they had a big range. And for the moment I thought that they were firing at us from tanks and that they had the intention to kill us and that I would get killed on the first day. But luckily I didn't get killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And in fact you were fighting the Serb police, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, against the Serb police and the Serb military -- army. They were fighting against us, and we responded to that fire as much as we could to our own means.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And you say that you went to Lapusnik two or three times --

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: -- to report. And that was to report to Fehmi Lladrovci. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And besides those two or three times that you went to Lapusnik to report, you also say you went there on other occasions to take guns with Islami. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes. I did not take the weapons with Islam there. I usually would take the weapons myself because, to my opinion, it was better to get killed myself in case I was ambushed by the Serbs. He would find persons he knew who had weapons. And as for bringing them, I would bring them myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And can I ask, where did you take these weapons in Lapusnik? Where did you actually hand them over?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Sorry. Perhaps I wasn't clear. You took some weapons to Lapusnik. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And these weapons Islam Qadraku -- sorry, and Islam Qadraku gave you these weapons. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: He did not give me the weapons. He knew people who were dealing with weapons, and he spoke with them. I would wait in a cafeteria or somewhere so that nobody would find out I was a member, because I would at that case say goodbye to this life. I would wait at a tea shop. And when he would finish business, he will say, Go with this person, take a weapon or two. Then I would take the weapon. Once I was with him and I suffered with -- from the police forces because of this. So I said to him that he should give me a person who we could trust so that I had no other problems. I was forced to take my wife with me so that I would not make the Serbs suspicious. On two or three occasions I went with my wife. I had weapons with me, and the Serbs didn't stop me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Who did you give these weapons to in Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes. I gave these weapons to Ymer Alushani, and I said to him, This weapon was bought. I don't know where Islam took it, but I'm the person who brought it to your door. And he would reply, Thank you very much. You have just armed another soldier of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And during all these trips to Lapusnik, you never became aware of any place where people were being kept, where people were being detained. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I don't understand you. On the road to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, despite these trips to Lapusnik and despite being involved in the KLA, you never heard that there was a prison in Lapusnik, did you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I had no chance to hear such words, as I mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Because I would just leave the weapon there and would not stay there any longer. Maybe all together 10, 15 minutes I would stay there and then leave for Blinaje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes. And it's fair, isn't it, that in your dealings with commanders at Lapusnik you dealt with Fehmi Lladrovci, Ymer Alushani, and then on one occasion Isak Musliu. You never dealt with Fatmir Limaj, did you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: That's how it was because I had no chance to meet Fatmir Limaj there and I don't remember meeting Isak Musliu. Maybe we took part in the same fighting and I didn't know. As I said before, we were not allowed to ask amongst ourself who was who.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And in fact you never heard about Commander Celiku until July 1998. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: That's how it was. When I returned to Blinaje and when he unarmed me, it's then that I knew him as Commander Celiku.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your overriding concern was to be involved in the battle and in the actions against the Serbs. Isn't that correct? What was what you wanted more than anything else?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was. And I was never known for other things. They were always known for such things to occupy us and to keep us under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And you listened to anybody who was called commander, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: It's not clear to me, anybody. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: You say that you learned Fatmir Limaj was a commander by listening to Mr. Black and other people, is that right? That he was a commander of a brigade. You learned that from Mr. Black and other people?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Who is Mr. Black? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Mr. Black is the gentleman that was asking you questions. Did you mean it when you said that you learnt that Mr. Limaj was a commander of a brigade because you learnt it from Mr. Black and other people in Kosova?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we read what exactly he said because I believe he said "speaking to me and his friends." I'd like to have the language that the witness actually used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I can move on. I'm not belabouring the point. It's neither here nor there, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. You're encouraged to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: You heard, you say, that Shukri -- Fatmir Limaj, Commander Celiku, was a superior of Shukri Buja. You heard that, you say?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I did not say -- I'm sorry, Mr. Black, for not remembering your name, but I said that I heard about Fatmir Limaj when those who were senior to us soldiers, including here Fatmir Limaj and Thaqi and many others, not to mention them by name, but it's then when I knew that Fatmir Limaj was Celiku. I can say that it was within this time frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And are you aware that Fatmir Limaj became the commander of the 121st Brigade in August 1998? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I don't know what happened in August or in any other months, but I know that he was commander of the 121st Brigade at the time that I referred to. For me, it wasn't a big deal who became commander and at what time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: You said you had some difficulties in understanding the attempts to organise the KLA. For example you didn't understand Commander Blini when he was describing that he was an operational commander. You were quite candid about that, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Are you aware that Fatmir Limaj was never at any time the commander or the superior of Shukri Buja? Would you agree with me that that's the case?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: You have no direct basis for saying that Mr. Limaj was ever the superior commander of Shukri Buja, do you? He was never a superior of Shukri Buja, he never gave orders to Shukri Buja, did he, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: To my knowledge, he did not give orders to Shukri Buja or to someone else. But I also know that someone gave someone else orders at that time. As I said before, I didn't deal with such matters as to who was giving orders to whom. I knew that perhaps there was a great man leading the KLA and who would lead us the way to freedom and who would bring freedom to the entire population of Kosova. And I would like to add, if I'm allowed to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Please. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: -- I'm very sad to see these gentlemen here because I respected them and I don't think they dealt with such things. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Are you aware that later on in the conflict Shukri Buja was the commander in the Nerodime zone after August of 1998? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I heard from my friends when the combat was going on in Nerodime zone, I heard about Shukri Buja being the commander there. I had not been for such a long time in Blinaje, and then my friends told me he went to the zone where he operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And in fact I think that Shukri Buja became involved in the Nerodime zone sometime before August 1998. Can you comment on that or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Sorry, am I to be mistaken here? Although I've taken the oath here to speak the truth and for me the truth is to speak of things that I've seen and things that I know. As for Shukri Buja, what he did there, I don't know because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Are you aware that after August Mr. Limaj's responsibilities after August 1998, his responsibilities were focused in the Pastrik zone, a different zone? Are you aware of that or you can't comment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I have no comment on this. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes. And you say that when you met Mr. Limaj in your village, your gun -- your weapon -- let me put it again. It's very badly put. You say when you met Mr. Limaj in your village he told you not to hold a weapon for 15 days. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not know that he was this person. I just knew that a commander was disarming me; that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And could that meeting in fact have taken place at the end of July 1998?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: I don't know when it happened. As I said earlier, it was a week or two after my return to Blinaje. I can't say for sure, but it was around this time when I returned to Blinaje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And I think you say that despite the order or the instruction that you were to put your weapon down for 15 days, you in fact, unknown to Mr. Limaj, were given your weapon back after nine days. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL KASTRATI
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes, if you could wait there; I'm very grateful?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Just a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Kastrati, I represent Isak Musliu, who you would have known only by the name of Qerqiz. All right. A few questions for you. First of all, geography. I wonder, could you have the map back, please, and could you have map 5 in front of you. Let's have it on the ELMO, if we may, because I want you to see if you can identify where your village is on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
